---
title: "phibble for Laravel developers"
---

phibble works with Laravel without configuration. Its service provider is
registered by package discovery, and it adds two kinds of macro:

- `->toDataFrame()` on collections and query builders runs the query and returns
  an in-memory `DataFrame`.
- `->phibble()` on query builders, Eloquent builders, and relations returns a
  lazy `SqlTable` on the query's connection. Verbs given expressions compile
  to SQL, so grouping and summarising run in the database.

Laravel is not a dependency. The examples on this page use Eloquent with an
in-memory SQLite database that holds the `penguins` data, through a model with a
`measured()` scope that keeps rows with a body mass.

## From a collection or query to a DataFrame

`toDataFrame()` builds a data frame from the rows of a collection or a query. Column
types are inferred from the values, as for `DataFrame::fromRows()`.

{{< include examples/_laravel-to-dataframe.md >}}

A collection of models becomes rows of their attributes. Eloquent casts and
accessors apply only when the models are loaded first, as in the example
above; `Penguin::query()->toDataFrame()` reads the rows directly.

## Queries that stay in the database

`phibble()` turns a builder into a lazy table. The builder's SQL, bindings,
and scopes become the table's source, and phibble's verbs add to that query.
Nothing runs until the rows are needed, for example with `collect()`, printing,
or `nrow()`.

{{< include examples/_laravel-phibble.md >}}

Global scopes such as `SoftDeletes` apply, because phibble reads the query
through Eloquent's `toBase()`. Attribute casts and accessors do not apply,
because the rows come from SQL.

`showQuery()` returns the SQL that `collect()` would run. In this example a
grouped filter keeps the heaviest penguin on each island. The comparison with
the group maximum compiles to a window function:

{{< include examples/_laravel-show-query.md >}}

Expressions that SQL cannot evaluate exactly as R does, and any PHP closure,
make the table collect its rows and continue in memory. The result is then a
`DataFrame`, and the values are the same as if the whole pipeline had run in
memory. The [SQL tables](sql.qmd) page lists these cases.

## With phplyr

[phplyr](https://github.com/phpstats/phplyr) provides dplyr's verbs as a
method chain on any PHP version and as functions for PHP 8.5's pipe operator.
Its verbs call the same table methods, so a phplyr pipeline on `phibble()` also
runs in the database:

::: {.panel-tabset group="syntax"}
## Method chain (PHP 8.3+)

```php
use function Phplyr\{phplyr, desc, n, mean};

$summary = phplyr(Penguin::query()->phibble())
    ->filter(col('year')->ge(2008))
    ->group_by('species', 'sex')
    ->summarise(n: n(), mass: mean(col('body_mass'), na_rm: true))
    ->arrange(desc('mass'))
    ->get();
```

## Pipe (PHP 8.5)

```php
use function Phplyr\{filter, group_by, summarise, arrange, desc, n, mean};

$summary = Penguin::query()->phibble()
    |> filter(col('year')->ge(2008))
    |> group_by('species', 'sex')
    |> summarise(n: n(), mass: mean(col('body_mass'), na_rm: true))
    |> arrange(desc('mass'));
```
:::

## Charts with phiz

[phiz](https://phpstats.github.io/phiz/) is a grammar of graphics in the
style of ggplot2 that produces Vega-Lite specifications. `Plot::of()` accepts
a phibble DataFrame directly. A query can select the needed columns in the
database, collect them, and plot them:

{{< include examples/_laravel-chart.md >}}

For a summary, the grouping and aggregation can also run in the database, so
only the summary rows reach PHP:

{{< include examples/_laravel-chart-summary.md >}}

In a Laravel view, phiz's Blade component renders a plot, and `@phizScripts`
loads the Vega libraries once per page:

```blade
<x-phiz :plot="$plot" />

@phizScripts
```

phiz also has helpers that plot phit model results, such as
`coefplot($fit)` and `effect_plot($fit, $data, 'x', by: 'g')`. Its
documentation covers them.

## Using the result

A collected data frame can be returned from a controller or passed to a view:

- `$df->toRows()` gives a list of associative arrays, for JSON responses
  and Blade loops.
- `$df->toJson()` gives the same rows as a JSON string, or the columns with
  `toJson('columns')`.
- `$df->toCollection()` returns a Laravel collection of rows.
- `$df->toModelData()` gives the columns in the form phit's model
  functions accept.
